title: CmdPal: Dock disappears when opening Action Center
author: niels9001

judgment.rationale: The issue gives an exact interaction: opening Windows Action Center hides the Dock, which does not return normally until focus moves elsewhere. The Command Palette Dock uses Windows AppBar/window management, but no evidence yet shows whether Action Center changes its visibility, z-order, or focus state.
evidence: The current Command Palette development build is reported on a laptop.
Opening Windows Action Center makes the Dock disappear; closing it and moving focus outside restores it.
There are no comments, attachments, or linked fixes.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the Action Center interaction and observe Dock visibility, z-order, and AppBar state while opening and closing the panel.

fix_assessment.rationale: A transient shell-window activation or z-order change may leave the Dock hidden, but the report does not identify whether the Dock hides itself, loses its AppBar state, or is occluded by the Windows panel.

proposed_fixes.title: Restore Command Palette Dock visibility after Action Center closes
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Opening Windows Action Center may change shell activation or z-order in a way that hides or occludes the Dock; the Dock's AppBar/window state may not be restored until another focus transition occurs.
plan: Reproduce the sequence and distinguish an actually hidden Dock window from one that remains visible but is occluded or behind another surface.
Trace Dock/AppBar activation and visibility transitions while Action Center opens and closes, including the point at which moving focus outside causes the Dock to return.
If the Dock's own visibility or AppBar state is not restored, update the relevant shell/window transition handling and add a regression test for Action Center open/close.
verification: Open and close Windows Action Center with the Dock enabled and confirm the Dock remains visible or is restored immediately when Action Center closes.
Verify ordinary focus changes and Command Palette Dock interactions continue to work without repeatedly forcing the Dock to the foreground.

confidence.rationale: The interaction is clearly reproducible, but the report does not distinguish hidden, occluded, or focus-delayed states; the AppBar source identifies ownership, not cause.

issue_context.summary: Opening Windows Action Center makes the Command Palette Dock disappear, and it does not return normally until focus moves outside Action Center.
known_information: The report concerns the current Command Palette development build on a laptop.
The stated interaction is enabling the Dock, opening Action Center, then closing it and returning focus to the desktop or another window.
The issue has no comments or attachments.
Current DockWindow source documents Windows AppBar work-area/position management; DockWindowManager manages the Dock windows.
inferences: Action Center may alter the Dock's window visibility, z-order, or focus state, but the report does not distinguish an actual hide from occlusion.
The delayed return after focus moves suggests the relevant recovery may be tied to a later activation transition, but this is not yet confirmed.
issue_context.analysis: The interaction is specific enough for a maintainer reproduction. Because the observed disappearance could be a hidden window, z-order occlusion, or focus state, first observe the Dock/AppBar state through Action Center open/close rather than immediately forcing it to the foreground.
initial_investigation: Inspected current Command Palette Dock source ownership: DockWindow.xaml.cs uses Windows AppBar/window APIs, and DockWindowManager.cs manages the Dock windows.
The separate #51014 Dev Box report shares the Dock owner but describes content overlap rather than a disappearance after a shell-panel transition; it is related, not a duplicate.
The issue has no comments, attachments, or linked fix reference.

related_issues.relationship: Separate Command Palette Dock overlap issue with a maximized Dev Box window; shared Dock owner but a different trigger and symptom.

reproduce.title: Test Dock visibility around Action Center
reproduce.version_requirement: Current Command Palette development build, as reported
prerequisites: Run the Command Palette Dock on a Windows laptop with Action Center available.
steps: Enable and show the Command Palette Dock.
Open Windows Action Center and observe whether the Dock disappears or is covered.
Close Action Center without moving focus to another window and check whether the Dock returns.
Move focus outside Action Center as described in the issue and observe whether that restores the Dock.
Compare the Dock window's visibility and z-order across these transitions.
reproduce.expected_result: The Dock remains visible or returns immediately when Action Center closes, without requiring an unrelated focus change.
reproduce.actual_to_confirm: Whether the Dock window is hidden, merely occluded, or left in a stale AppBar/focus state until another activation event.
